New Crypto Futures Exchanges in 2026: How to Evaluate Them Before You Deposit

Guides · 7 min read · Updated June 2026

Every cycle brings a wave of new trading platforms. Some become the next giants — early Bybit users remember when it was the newcomer — and some disappear with deposits. This is the evaluation checklist we use before covering any new exchange, the red flags that end the conversation, and how to be positioned early without taking platform risk. (This page is updated as notable platforms launch. Educational only — not financial advice.)

Why early users get the best deal

Launch-window promotions are usually the most generous an exchange will ever run: deposit bonuses, zero-fee windows, trading competitions with thin competition. Exchanges spend heavily to seed liquidity and users in the first months — being early, with correct sizing, is a real edge. The catch is that you are also early to the platform risk, which is why the checklist below exists.

The 7-point checklist before you deposit

  • 1. Withdrawals first. Small deposit, one trade, withdraw everything. If a withdrawal takes days or needs support tickets in week one, walk away.
  • 2. Who runs it. Public team with names and history beats an anonymous one. Registration/jurisdiction should be findable in minutes.
  • 3. Fees — the whole schedule. Maker/taker is the headline; funding intervals, withdrawal fees and hidden spreads are where new platforms pad margins. Compare against the established exchanges.
  • 4. Real liquidity. Open the order book on the pairs you trade. Thin books mean slippage and stop-hunts — volume numbers can be painted, depth is harder to fake.
  • 5. Liquidation mechanics. Margin tiers, maintenance-margin rates and auto-deleveraging rules must be documented. Know your liquidation price before the first leveraged trade.
  • 6. Proof of reserves. After 2022, any serious platform publishes reserves or a credible audit. None = your deposit is an unsecured loan.
  • 7. The bonus fine print. Launch bonuses often lock withdrawals behind volume requirements. Read the terms before the deposit, not after.

Red flags that end the evaluation

Guaranteed returns anywhere on the site. Withdrawal minimums that trap small accounts. Anonymous team plus aggressive influencer marketing. Fee schedule that requires support to explain. Any pressure to deposit before you can see the trading interface.

Be ready before you are exposed

The smart sequence: learn the mechanics risk-free on Paper Trade (live prices, leverage, liquidation — no money), keep your sizing rules from the position-size guide, and when a new platform passes the checklist, start with a test deposit you can afford to lose entirely.
